#4730. The 10 Most Comfortable Bras, According to Style Editors

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

I’ve tested more bras than I can count as a style writer. And over the years, I’ve learned that comfort is a nonnegotiable—if it digs, pinches, or rides up, it doesn’t deserve a space in my drawer. The thing is, no two boobs are exactly alike (not even your own). One might sit higher, be fuller, or have a different shape than the other. So finding the right bra isn’t about hitting a standard size—it’s about understanding your body. According to Navya Mysore, MD, a primary care physician and Women’s Health advisor, the right bra boosts comfort, improves posture, and eases back pain by evenly distributing breast tissue. If your band rides up, your straps slide, or your underwire doesn’t lie flat, it’s a clear sign something’s off.

And if your usual size suddenly stops working? Totally normal. Bra fitter and undergarment educator Kimmay Caldwell says weight changes, hormone shifts, or your monthly cycle can impact your size. To make it trickier, some brands still use outdated sizing methods (like the “plus four” rule), while others go by your exact underbust. Bottom line: your size can change and vary between clothing brands.

All of that can make bra shopping feel like a bit of a minefield, which is exactly why I tested 20 different styles across fits, fabrics, and support levels to find the ones that are actually worth your money. These ten passed the wear test and then some, proving that comfort, support, and style actually can exist in one bra.

A bra should fit your body—not the other way around—and Knix totally got the memo with this one. It feels snug at first, but it softens and molds to your shape with every wear. What really impressed me was the fit because it almost feels custom, thanks to the ultra-thin foam that contours without adding volume.

Plus, the sleek fabric (a nylon-spandex blend) moves with you, feeling super smooth against the skin and breathable enough to wear for hours.

If you're after definition without the discomfort, this wire-free option def delivers. The molded cups lift and separate, while subtle side padding helps prevent spillage and sideboob. The result? A natural shape, no extra bulk, and no awkward lines under tighter tops. And with 99 sizes (!!) and eight colors, the options are actually inclusive.

The only downside? It’s not the best for high movement and workouts. I find myself adjusting it when I bend or move quickly. Still, for everyday comfort and a super flattering fit, this one’s a standout.

If you love the shape and support of a traditional bra but can't stand the feel of underwire, the Shapermint Essentials Sweetheart Wireless Contour Bra is your happy medium. It delivers a surprisingly lifted, rounded silhouette without a single wire digging into your ribs, making it my top pick for anyone who wants all-day comfort.

The lightly contoured foam cups provide just enough structure to prevent the dreaded uniboob, while the wide, stretchy band stays comfortably in place without pinching or rolling. The smooth, buttery fabric feels soft against the skin and disappears nicely under T-shirts and other fitted tops.

I was especially impressed by how supportive it feels for a wireless bra. It lifts and shapes without feeling restrictive, and the wider straps help distribute weight so your shoulders don't pay the price after hours of wear. It's one of those bras you forget you're wearing—which is pretty much the highest compliment I can give.

Push-up bras with underwires have a bad rep, and for good reason. They’re usually stiff, pokey, and downright uncomfortable. But after wearing this Maidenform bra for months (yes, months), I can confidently say it’s a major exception to the rule.

From the start, this bra felt different. The underwire doesn’t dig or jab, thanks to its soft, stretchy crochet lace that moves with you. The cups are unpadded but still offer that ideal medium support and lift, enough to give shape and a gentle push-up effect, but never so much that I feel squeezed or overly sculpted. It’s supportive without being suffocating, which is rare in the world of push-ups.And let’s talk about the straps. They’re fully adjustable and convertible, so whether I’m going for a classic or criss-cross fit, I can tweak the style to match my outfit. That kind of versatility makes it feel like you’re getting two bras in one (and who doesn’t love a multitasker?).The lift it gives is subtle but effective. It’s not the dramatic “hello, cleavage” kind of push-up, but more of a natural, perky boost that works under everything from tees to low-cut dresses. No spillage, just a flattering shape that makes me feel more confident in whatever I’m wearing. Bonus points for the range of styles: It comes in smooth fabric options to wear under clingy tees, and lace versions for when you want to have a little more fun.One of my biggest bra fears? The dreaded back and side bulge. But this bra’s smoothing side panels genuinely help—there’s no weird digging or over-compression, just a smooth, flattering fit that doesn’t fight with your body. Long story short: I tested it, I lived in it, and I’m keeping it in my regular rotation.

As someone who hates wearing bras (the wires, the bulk, the digging), this is the one I wear most. Made for fuller busts (DD+), the Cosabella Evolution Curvy Bralette lifts and shapes with lightly molded cups, no wires necessary.

“It’s the only bralette I’ve found that can actually support my chest without feeling restrictive,” says style contributor Lily Wohlner. The soft, stretchy fabric, made from a smooth microfiber that consists of 85 percent polyamide and 15 percent elastane, molds to your body, starting snug and quickly adapting for a custom-like fit. “I will say, mine have stretched a bit over the past few years, so it might be time to re-up,” she says.

This bra provides exceptional support for larger busts, even without a heavy-duty wire band. Instead, it makes use of an elasticized band that provides a surprisingly large amount of support without digging into the skin. It also has extra support at the sides to prevent spillage and to keep everything looking seamless, even under thin t-shirts and tight dresses.

The adjustable straps and underband stay put, and the side coverage smooths everything out—no spillage, no weird lines under shirts. It gives a natural, rounded shape that works under pretty much anything.

If you tend to scoop the girls into place to make them look perkier (a good trick!), this Cuup bra does the work for you. The rounded neckline and unlined, unpadded cups naturally lift and shape, while seamlessly extending into the straps for clean lines and a flattering fit.

It runs snug, but that’s what makes it so supportive—my boobs stay put and look perkier without any adjusting. The underwire is super lightweight and flexible, so there’s zero digging or poking there. I also love that the cups are unlined, because it makes the bra feel super lightweight and barely there.

The bra is made from a microfiber blend of polyamide and elastane, so it’s buttery-smooth, stretches with you while keeping its shape, and is ultra-breathable. It’s great for warm days since it feels like next to nothing on the skin and helps wick moisture away. The microfiber is also great for pairing with thin or tight tops, since it's basically undetectable under clothing—no lines in sight.

The straps are fully adjustable for a customizable lift, and even though the cups are thin, they still offer enough coverage to prevent any chilly-day surprises, IYKYK. Since the cups run a bit small, sizing up might be your best bet for full coverage.

The Honeylove CrossOver Bra is ultra-comfortable, smoothing, and supportive. The nylon and spandex blend feels soft and wearable for hours without digging into your skin while providing a completely seamless silhouette from every angle. I always wear this pick under thinner tops, tight dresses, and clingy sweaters because it creates a totally streamlined look under clothes while lifting the girls and supporting the underarm area and sides.

Plus, the bonded cradle under the bust mimics the structure of an underwire, delivering firm support without any poking or pinching. The full mesh overlay adds light compression and lift, adding to the sleek look.

“The CrossOver bra feels like a sports bra on, which is especially handy for women in search of something extra-comfortable (hi),” says contributor Korin Miller, who wore this bra every day for nearly a month to see how well it performed. She appreciates the flexible boning at the sides of the cups to prevent sideboob and bulging.

This bra also has one of the widest size ranges on our list, which is a major win. However, it does run a little big, so if you're between sizes, consider sizing down for the best fit.

Read More: Honeylove CrossOver Bra Review

Finding a lace bra that's actually comfortable—especially if you have a larger bust—can feel like a tall order, but the Bravissimo Millie Bra proves you don't have to sacrifice support for something pretty. It's my top pick for fuller busts thanks to its soft stretch lace cups, which mold to your shape for a flexible, barely-there feel instead of digging in or gaping.

Unlike stiff, scratchy lace bras, this one feels surprisingly comfortable from the first wear. The unpadded cups hug your breasts without adding bulk, while the stretchy lace adapts to your natural shape for a fit that feels supportive without being restrictive. The delicate floral lace also gives it an elevated, feminine look that's pretty enough to show off under a slightly unbuttoned blouse or low-cut top.

Meanwhile, the side sling creates a naturally lifted, forward shape, and if you wear a JJ or K cup, those sizes include additional lining for even more support where you need it most. The result is a flattering silhouette that feels secure without relying on heavy padding.

The only catch is that it's designed specifically for fuller busts, so sizing starts at a D cup.

The Natori Bliss Perfection Bra nails the perfect balance of comfort and structure. It feels light and flexible but keeps everything perfectly lifted and in place. No readjusting is needed halfway through the day, as is so often the case. That's thanks to the stretchy fabric, fully adjustable straps and band, and the strong yet plush underwire.

The smooth microfiber fabric (a nylon and spandex blend) feels buttery-soft against the skin, with just enough stretch to move as you do. Even the lace trim—sometimes a red flag for irritation—is whisper-smooth and lies flat under clothes. And while there’s an underwire, it’s so well-cushioned that it supports without poking or digging.

It’s the only underwire bra I don’t rip off the second I get home. It’s really the only bra I reach for when I head to the office or if I’m wearing a top that requires a little more lift and support for that flattering look. Style-wise, it looks as good as it feels. The lightly-lined cups create a natural, rounded shape that disappears under everything from fitted tees to silk blouses, and the smooth band keeps the silhouette seamless.

Our only con? It’s handwash only. I tried washing mine in a mesh laundry bag the first time it needed a clean, and while it wasn’t destroyed, it definitely pilled a bit.

If you have a smaller bust, you don't need a ton of padding to get a flattering fit—and the Journelle Victory Plunge Bra is proof. It's my top pick for A- to C-cups thanks to its lightly structured, unlined design that hugs your natural shape while disappearing under clothes.

The contoured cups mold to your body for a smooth, comfortable fit, and because they lie completely flat, there's no bunching or gaping to contend with. Despite having zero padding, the cups still provide full nipple coverage, so you get a sleek look under even the clingiest t-shirts without adding extra bulk.

I also appreciate that the plunge neckline works under just about everything, from V-necks to lower-cut tops, while the underwire offers just enough lift to create a naturally rounded shape. The result is polished and supportive without looking overly structured.

The only drawback is that it's best suited to smaller busts, as it doesn't offer the level of coverage or support many fuller busts need. But it is available up to a G cup if you’d like to try it out yourself.

If you love a deep V-neckline but hate when your bra peeks out, meet your new go-to: the Harper Wilde Bliss Triangle Bralette. It’s made with a flattering plunge that stays supportive and hidden under low-cut tops and dresses. I’ve worn it under everything from wrap dresses to tanks and it disappears under all of them. The triangle shape gives a natural lift—no wires, no padding, just your boobs but sliiightly perkier.

Comfort-wise, it lives up to the name. The modal fabric is buttery-soft and stretchy in that live-in-it kind of way. The band is wide and smooth, so it stays put without digging, and the adjustable straps let you customize the fit. It’s also lightweight enough to forget you’re even wearing it.

It’s become my go-to for daily wear, and the super-soft, barely-there material is truly the next best thing to going bra-free. While it’s equally great for bed-rotting or taking Zoom calls from home, I also feel confident wearing it out and about because it doesn’t skimp on coverage and offers just enough support.

Even without padding, the double-layered fabric gives solid nipple coverage. It comes in inclusive sizes and neutral shades that go with everything. The few cons? It’s not super supportive for heavy movement or fuller busts, so you may need to readjust on the go. But for everyday wear, especially with low-cut outfits, it fits the bill.

The most comfortable bras usually come down to the right blend of fabrics. Here’s what each one brings to the table:

Comfort is about more than just size—it’s also about ensuring the wire doesn’t create pressure points or cause discomfort throughout the day. Look for bras with flexible, padded, or cushioned underwires, which offer support without digging into your skin. The underwire should sit flat against your ribcage and follow the natural curve of your breasts. If it feels like it’s poking or shifting, it’s not the right fit. If you prefer a wire-free bra, opt for styles with flexible boning, molded cups, and wide, flexible bands to provide support.

The most accurate way to find your size is to get fitted in person. Once you have your size, your new bra should feel snug and secure. The band should be comfortably tight, but not dig into the skin. A good rule of thumb is that you should be able to fit two fingers between the band and your skin, but no more. The cups should also lie flat against your chest.

The Women’s Health team has been testing bras since we first wrote this story in 2023. To find the most comfortable options, our team wore each style for at least a few weeks at a time. We wore them under different circumstances, including workouts, lounging, and long days at the office. But our main criterion for each bra was comfort. I also spoke with two bra experts and personally tested 20-plus bras over several years to lock down the ones I actually wear on repeat.

I recently re-tested a bunch of options and tapped style contributor Lily Wohlner for an update to this story to boost our list and keep it up-to-date. The final guide includes everything from bralettes and seamless bras to push-up bras—and I actually wear all of them in my day-to-day life.

#4729. E-quipment highlight: Jungheinrich launches new forklift for Asian markets

Like many equipment brands, German forklift maker Jungheinrich has been struggling to crack the Asian industrial markets – but the company is set to change all that with the launch of a new line of 1.6- to 3-ton class electric forklifts designed specifically to navigate the region’s tight warehouses and factories.

Jungheinrich launched the next generation of its EFG MB and MC electric counterbalance forklifts, giving businesses more flexibility to match truck performance with the battery options, charging systems, and operator features that meet their specific needs.

“Different operations have different requirements,” said Lisa Jing Xue, Managing Director at Jungheinrich’s Qingpu Plant, China. “With the EFG M series, customers can configure the (forklift) truck around their application, workload and operators – whether they need greater maneuverability for confined warehouse spaces, or a stable, powerful truck for demanding transport and stacking work.”

Forklift buyers can choose between two performance packages, prioritizing energy efficiency for everyday material handling or more driving and lifting muscle for more demanding, high-throughput operations. The higher-performance package comes standard on models rated for 2.5-3.0 tons, with a choice of either lead-acid or lithium-ion batteries with 346 or 690 Ah of capacity available to suit different workloads and shift patterns. Both ship with regenerative braking tech that can recover up to 30% of the energy used in stopping and lowering loads, too, helping to keep these machines running longer between charging sessions.

“We carried out extensive customer research to understand what the market needs,” added Jing Xue. “Customers can invest in the performance required today and add further capabilities as their application demands.”

Optional features include fingertip controls, a larger 4″ digital display, upgraded LED lighting, and operator-assistance (ADAS) systems, while flexible seating and cabin configurations are designed to keep drivers comfortable through long shifts. A slim B-pillar and glass roof help visibility in busy warehouses, while the four-wheel EFG MC gets automatic cornering speed reduction as standard. Integrated telematics are also standard, giving fleet managers access to utilization data, maintenance planning and pre-operational checks from day one.

Jungheinrich says the order books for both the three- and four-wheel electric forklifts are open now, ready to be supported by the company’s 6,000+ person strong service network across the Asia-Pacific region.

#4728. The 7 Best Electric Toothbrushes for Men in 2026, Tested by Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Cleaner, healthier teeth with picks for every budget and style of brushing.

YOU ALREADY KNOW you need to brush at least twice a day, no matter what toothpaste or mouthwash you use. But technique matters just as much. Even for me—a grooming editor who writes about this stuff—it can feel like a chore. In the morning, I brush before coffee when I’m barely awake. At night, I’m wiped out from the day or drifting off for less wholesome reasons. That’s why I love electric toothbrushes: they simplify brushing and deliver a better clean by doing most of the work for you.

Unlike manual toothbrushes, electric toothbrushes use vibrations and automated head movement to remove plaque and debris. Many models include smart programs for whitening or gum care, interchangeable heads for sensitive or deep cleaning, and built-in timers. Some of the latest options even feature AI that tracks your brushing and suggests improvements.

But the main selling point of electric toothbrushes is their ability to clean more thoroughly and efficiently than manual options, using power and vibrations no hand can match. Top-tier electric toothbrushes can be pricey, but they’re an investment in your smile. It’s the closest you can get to a dentist-level clean at home.

For the past two years, the Oral-B Series 10 has been listed at the top of this list. It remains the best overall electric toothbrush; however, it’s currently sold out everywhere due to this demand. The model that immediately preceded it, the iO Series 9, is the next best thing. It features many of the same features and power, just with a less high-tech charging mount (which may be a benefit for some who prefer something lighter and less complicated).

Series 9 is similarly a premium electric toothbrush packed with advanced features designed to elevate your oral care routine. Just like the 10, there are seven customizable modes—including Daily Clean, Sensitive, Super Sensitive, Intense, Gum Care, Tongue Clean, and Whitening—this brush adapts to your needs, whether you have sensitive gums or want a deep clean. Its oscillating, vibrating round brush head provides a powerful yet gentle clean, and the built-in pressure sensor ensures you're brushing with the right amount of force, lighting up red (too strong), blue (too weak), or green (just right) based on your pressure.

The Series 9 pairs with a companion app to track your brushing in real time across 16 zones of the mouth, offering instant feedback and a visual map of missed areas. I’m not a huge tech junkie, especially when it comes to something like brushing my teeth, since I just want to get it over with quickly. But this is one of the few apps that genuinely adds value, with accurate tracking, clear visuals, and brushing reminders.

Even if you skip the app, the built-in display shows your selected mode and a timer, though the latter is easier to read in the app. That being said, it’s nearly impossible to achieve a 100 percent clean according to the app (I usually aim for between 80 and 90) without brushing for five or more minutes, which is not recommended because it can damage enamel. If you’re a perfectionist, this will prove annoying.

In terms of design, the Series 9 is sleek and solid, and comes with a sturdy travel case. It charges in just three hours (significantly faster than most others on this list) and comes with four replacement heads, which should cover your first year of use if you replace them every three months, as dentists advise.

If you prefer sonic, this toothbrush offers nearly the same level of features and effectiveness as the Oral-B iO Series 9. At $340, it's also one of the most expensive electric toothbrushes, but the price includes five modes and three intensity settings to fully customize your brushing experience, along with an innovative charging cup.

Interchangeable brush heads, specifically designed for tasks like whitening or tongue cleaning, also help you achieve optimal results with minimal effort. Similar to the Series 9, it also has app-enabled smart modes that provide personalized feedback on your brushing habits and overall progress. Plus, the charging travel case makes it easy to travel while protecting your investment.

Women’s Health Associate Style and Commerce Editor Shannen Zitz has been using this toothbrush for the past year and says it’s the cleanest her teeth have ever felt. “I’ve long been using an electric toothbrush, so I didn’t expect to be too blown away by this one. I was wrong.” She likes how it pairs multiple brush heads, cleaning modes, and a timer with real-time app feedback to keep her brushing technique on track. The sleek charging cup also makes storage and charging effortless, even on a tiny sink, she says.

Read More: Are Electric Toothbrushes Better?

Men’s Health Associate Producer Janie Booth says the round, oscillating head reminds her of the tool dental hygienists use to polish teeth during a professional cleaning. The brush comes with a compact stand and a travel case, both of which are easy to pack. It doesn’t include a wall plug—just a USB cord—but the battery lasts impressively long.

Booth says she’s used it for a month without recharging once. If your biggest concern is avoiding charging as much as possible, the Rev is your best bet. The battery even outperforms the Oral-B iO Series 9 and Philips Sonicare DiamondClean, both of which are roughly $300 more expensive.

I’ve used all three as my daily driver at different times, and the Rev battery lasts at least a week longer. You can expect to get at least 5 weeks from a single full charge with twice-a-day use. The rest of its offerings are pretty minimal, though, again, this will be welcomed by newcomers. It only offers three levels of intensity, but none are too strong for sensitive teeth.

However, they’re not quite as powerful as the most intense settings on Oral-B and Philips, though they are close. The Oral-B iO Series 9 offers about 10,500 oscillations per minute on its Daily Clean setting, while the Rev goes up to 9,630 oscillations per minute. Considering the $300 price difference between the two, the slight dip is a worthy trade-off.

Before I upgraded to an electric, I was a devotee of Colgate’s Active Prevention Foaming Toothbrush. The heads are as soft as they come, and the handle fits perfectly in my hand. Naturally, I was thrilled when the brand made an electric version, adding vibration to those two core features. To be clear, this is battery-powered, so it’s not rechargeable. But you also don’t need to worry about recharging it every couple of weeks. I get a little more than a month out of each set of batteries (two AAAs), so while it’s under $15 at first, I plan to spend more over time.

Still, I haven’t tried a battery-powered toothbrush that lasts that long without sputtering or losing efficiency, like Colgate’s can. It’s not the most powerful electric toothbrush, as Colgate doesn’t even list its vibrations per minute (which usually means it’s nothing to write home about). But I’ve yet to find a battery-powered toothbrush that can compete with the power of rechargeable options, so it’s inherent to the design.

No matter your background, everyone shares one truth: we all lie to our dentists about flossing. They see through it, and they roll their eyes for good reason. Daily flossing is essential, which is why Waterpik built a toothbrush with an integrated water flosser. Its all-in-one design lets you brush and floss at the same time, saving effort while leaving your teeth feeling dentist-clean.

The brush includes two intensity modes and a timer, but the standout is the built-in Waterpik. You can brush with or without the water flosser, though why skip it? While it doesn’t offer the smart features of higher-end models, the unique water flosser justifies its higher price tag. Plus, its 30,000 vibrations per minute match those of the similarly priced Zina45. In that sense, it’s like the water flosser is free.

This toothbrush offers 33,000 vibrations per minute, four custom settings, a two-minute timer, and soft, nylon bristles. It’s everything you need for a decent electric toothbrush. However, there are two features that help it stand out. For one, the magnetic USB touch charger is super convenient, making recharging as simple as any option on this list. As someone who regularly forgets to recharge his devices, I appreciate how easy this one makes the process.

It also comes with a polishing head, one of the few electric toothbrushes that do. This tiny rubber head is designed to make your teeth look smoother and shinier by focusing on surface stains and plaque removal rather than deep cleaning between teeth. I use mine after brushing, even if I brush with a separate toothbrush, to complete the full at-home dentist-level clean. It also comes with four replaceable polishing heads, so you won’t have to worry about replacing them for some time.

At first, the smaller toothbrush head on the Suri 2.0 felt less effective than the OG model, but over time, it delivers the same clean. The brush comes with a compact stand and a travel case, both designed for travel. It doesn’t include a wall plug—just a USB cord—but the battery lasts impressively long. It’s the only other electric toothbrush we’ve tested that lasts over a month on a single charge, though I find it’s a couple of days shorter than the Quip Rev.

This brush delivers 33,000 vibrations per minute yet remains whisper-quiet. Its sleek case hides a UV-C light that kills 99 percent of germs on the brush head, keeping it clean wherever you take it. Plus, the head and bristles are eco-friendly, made from recyclable, plant-based cornstarch and castor oil. Overall, it’s powerful, sustainable, and travel-ready.

When choosing an electric toothbrush, you’ll need to decide between a sonic or oscillating brush head. There isn’t one right answer; it just comes down to preference.

Toothbrushes have gone smart, too. Most models include the basics—a strong motor and a built-in timer—but many now add extras like brushing modes, pressure sensors, and even AI to track your habits and coach you to improve. The right features depend on what matters most to you.

Brushing your teeth is personal, shaped by your own needs and quirks. To find the best electric toothbrushes for every sensitivity and style, we tapped a wide group of Men’s Health testers. I spoke with dentists about their go-to brands, pulled in feedback from our original 2019 guide, and compiled a list of top contenders. I then distributed these toothbrushes to writers and editors, each of whom tested them for at least a month to judge comfort, ease of use, and long-term effectiveness. Based on that feedback, here are the eight best electric toothbrushes for men in 2026.

As with manual toothbrushes, electric toothbrush heads need to be replaced every few months. Because the latter tend to be more expensive, this makes owning electric models more expensive. I recommend buying the heads in bulk when available, as this can make for pretty substantial savings. Electric toothbrushes have more nooks and crevices than their manual counterparts, which means they require a little extra daily maintenance.

This means carefully rinsing them after every use to stave off funky toothpaste and spit residue. It’s also worth actually removing the brush head from time to time to wipe the attachment point where the head meets the handle. A cotton swab or even your old toothbrush is usually enough to do the trick.

It’s tempting to just toss old toothbrushes and toothbrush heads in the trash once they’ve outlived their usefulness. But they’re actually perfect for detailed cleaning work that requires moderately stiff bristles to clean out tight spaces. Think: Shower heads, hiking boots, bathroom grout, your dishwasher filter, bird feeders—you get the idea.

#4727. 7 Best Moroccan Rugs (2026)

The Moroccan rug is one of the easiest ways to add texture and intrigue to any room. Originally made to protect floors against the harsh cold of the Atlas Mountains, we see these lush, woolly carpets as a staple in the modern design world because of the range of color and style options available. The rug type has become synonymous with traditional undyed cream colors, vibrant jewel tones, and geometric patterns. It’s no wonder they pop up across tons of our home tours—like this artful Brooklyn studio and floral Victorian house—and have become a favorite among artists like Claudio Bravo and celebs like Patrick Dempsey.

Boucherouite, the hand-weaving technique employed to make these rugs, was created by semi-nomadic Amazigh tribes, and the style can be found in abundance in the busy souks of Marrakech. Now, with many direct-to-consumer and vintage Beni Ourain-inspired styles on the market, the perfect Moroccan rug is just one click away. With all the options at your disposal, it may be intimidating to know where to start. Fear not, we’ve rounded up a few top picks below along with advice on how we’d style them.

Give your guests the coziest welcome with this Azilal rug from Revival Rugs. Its long, narrow design makes it ideal for tight entryways. And while the oblong diamond pattern speaks to geometric patterns you’ll see across traditional Moroccan rugs, the pink tassel is a niche, colorful detail that won’t overpower surrounding decor. This is an authentic hand-knotted Moroccan rug, with wool locally sourced from the Atlas Mountains. Because of its small size, you may also consider hanging it up to add a textural element to your wall decor.

Break up the monotony of home office decor by placing an eclectic rug under your desk setup. While the soft grey and subtle design still create a distraction-free workspace, the cheeky oxblood hues add a touch of personality to make you smile between emails and Zoom meetings.

You don’t have to get a custom carpet straight from Marrakesh to have a high-end rug. The Saira rug from Quince is a handwoven option at an affordable price. The geometric motif is heavily inspired by Moroccan design and the medium-pile, hand-spun wool is designed to feel plush under your feet.

Calling all maximalists and color drenchers. The rich, vibrant colors from this rug come from a family of third-generation dyers, and the irregular shapes of the boxes infuse a quirky texture to whatever room they are placed in. Either have this rug as the standout piece in a room that is otherwise neutral, or pair it with other green pieces like this couch from Ellison Studios to engulf yourself in a verdant indoor forest of your own making.

Even though this muted rug may look understated at first glance, it brings visual interest thanks to the grid design along the border. The motif takes inspiration from Mediterranean tile patterns, in case you were wondering. We can see this as a soft, elegant layer underneath your dining table. Water-resistant and machine washable, this rug can survive stains and spills without making you bat an eye.

Why should the adults have all the fun? Bring whimsical design to your child’s bedroom or playroom with this Moroccan area rug from Benisouk. We have a feeling that the high pile will feel comfy for the kids to run around on and durable enough to withstand a little wear and tear from playtime. The dreamy creamsicle hues of this rug can match youthful decor, but the abstract minimalist design is elevated enough to be a piece that grows with them through the years.

If you find yourself longing for sleek, beige interiors—or are in the midst of remodeling your home to mirror an Aman resort—look no further. This handmade sheep’s wool rug is a minimalist dream. The neutral cream brings a layer of calm, while the organic shapes offer a wabi-sabi element that may be necessary in a pristine white room.

#4726. The 10 Best Workout Tops for Women of 2026, Tested by Experts and Editors

Our fave option on this list is from Beyond Yoga.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

I’ve spent years logging miles, reps, and classes in all types of activewear; which means I’ve tested more workout tops than I can count. From Pilates to outdoor runs to heavy lifting sessions, I know exactly what separates a top you forget you’re wearing from one you can’t wait to peel off. For me, the best workout tops for women nail comfort, offer just enough support, and look flattering.

The last thing you want is an overly tight top that clips your movement (especially during yoga!), but it should still provide enough compression to hold you and the girls in, says Rebecca Stewart, CPT, a trainer and mobility coach. While you could make do with a regular cotton t-shirt during your workout sesh, it won't offer the same level of support, mobility, or sweat-wicking capabilities.

Finding the right workout top all comes down to personal preference. Because there are so many options to choose from—think T-shirts, tanks, and long-sleeve tops—we asked experts and tested tons of options ourselves to find styles we think will fit a wide range of needs and preferences. From lightweight, flowy options to compression shirts great for high-intensity workouts, our absolute favorite workout tops below are highlighted below.

Over the last few months I’ve tested a handful of workout tops and the Beyond Yoga Spacedye Slim Racerback Cropped Tank topped my list for a few reasons: It’s super comfortable (it won a spot for the softest bra in our Best Racerback Bras story!), has a built-in shelf bra, is size inclusive, and comes in a ton of vibrant and neutral shades.

It's basically the two-in-one bra and workout tank combo you didn’t know you needed. Made from the brand’s signature polyester and elastane blend, it’s the comfiest and most lightweight option I’ve ever worn. It feels like you're wearing nothing at all, but it still keeps the girls in place with a medium-level compression that’s perfect for light to moderate workouts. The cherry on top? It’s moisture-wicking, so it keeps you dry whether you’re working out or just running around on a hot day.

Our only gripe: If you have a bigger chest, you’ll probably want to layer a sports bra underneath for extra support. But if you're part of the itty bitty titty committee, you're good to go wearing this solo pretty much anywhere.

Read More: Beyond Yoga Spacedye Slim Racerback Tank Review

ICYMI, Amazon Essentials Activewear is where it’s at for affordable workout basics that rival the quality of some of the more luxe brands we’ve tried. The cotton, modal, and elastane blend feels thick, substantial, and smooth to the touch. It’s the kind of material that holds up well throughout repeated workouts and wash cycles, so you can keep this workout tee in constant rotation.

We also love the subtle crop length that isn’t too short or too long. It gives you room to move without showing too much skin, and has a semi-relaxed fit that perfectly skims the body. It’s extremely soft, but thanks to the touch of elastane in the fabric, it has ample stretch so you don’t feel constricted during overhead lifts or higher-impact workouts like running or HIIT.

The only con is that the white color can be slightly see-through. We suggest opting for a darker shade or wearing a flesh-toned bra underneath. The color options are also a little limited, but we love the slate gray and light blue options.

WH editors have tried a lot of workout tops over the years and agree that the Lululemon Ebb to Street Tank is a reliable favorite. It’s super soft, seamless, sweat-wicking, and ultra stretchy thanks to a comfortable blend of elastane and nylon. Plus, it offers just the right amount of support and coverage for low-impact workouts like Pilates, yoga, and walking.

The most convenient part: it has a built-in shelf bra, so you don’t have to wear a separate bra underneath (unless you want to for more support!). And, we found that it actually does keep us feeling covered and protected during low-impact exercise, which we didn’t find to be the case with other tanks that have built-in bras. Another pro? The longer length of this top (it hits at the hip) keeps us feeling locked in and covered during workouts where we don’t want a ton of stomach showing.

“I love how versatile this top is, along with its longer length and the buttery-soft blend of nylon and elastane,” says trainer Kristina Earnest, CPT, founder of Kristina Earnest On Demand. This is her go-to top when she's working out at home, and she wears it under a sweater for her cold weather errands. It feels incredibly comfortable thanks to its seamless racerback design—no pesky straps, seams, or tightness to get in the way during your sweat session. However, you should note that because there are no adjustable straps, you can't customize the fit of this tank.We put this tank to the test during a variety of workouts, like HIIT training and running, and found that it’s not the best choice for high-intensity training. We noticed that it didn’t do a great job of holding the breasts in place during high-impact moves and felt the need for more padding and compression. But based on our extensive testing, it's difficult to find a tank with high-impact support. That's why we recommend pairing this with our favorite high-impact sports bra, the Under Armour Infinity 2.0 High Sports Bra.

This tank is meant to be worn over your favorite sports bra as an added layer of coverage. The loose, cropped fit is easy to throw on, and the round neck with the knotted side detail adds a touch of style. Our fave part about this tank? The cotton material is super breathable, so you never feel overheated or constricted like you would with a tighter top.

“I love that this top isn’t too tight,” says Jacqueline Kasen, CPT, trainer and senior director of group fitness at Anatomy. “It’s super comfortable and loose whether you’re running or lifting, but it still stays in place without bunching up.” Plus, it holds its shape after multiple washes and never pills or frays, making it as durable as it is functional.

The tank is made with cotton, but it also has a bit of spandex woven throughout, which makes it stretchy and not too sturdy. This is essential during workouts, as you want your top to move with you instead of against you at the gym.

We noticed that the shirt can look a bit boxy if you go too oversized, so we recommend sizing down for a more flattering, snug fit.

This short-sleeve workout top from Under Armour is a game changer for high-intensity exercise since it offers both compression and cooling technology. It’s designed as a baselayer to keep you protected under your sports gear (by preventing pinching and chafing), but we love to wear it on its own as a temperature-regulating, sweat-wicking, ultra-lightweight workout top.

This t-shirt has an ultra-tight, compressive fit (which can help with circulation and muscular endurance), but it is super thin and made with the brand's HeatGear fabric to keep you from overheating. It’s made from polyester for a smooth, lightweight feel, plus elastane for a generous amount of stretch. We love that this top is breathable and moisture-wicking, so even though it’s on the tighter side, it doesn’t feel like you’re wearing anything. Whether you’re lifting heavy or doing sprints outdoors, this top is perfect for keeping you cool, dry, and comfortable.

However, this top (like most compressive gear) might not be the best option for lower-impact exercise or workouts that require lots of stretching and bending—like yoga or Pilates. We generally opt for looser, softer fits for these workouts and stick to tighter tops for strength training and cardio.

Listen, I love a cute lil workout set as much as the next Pilates princess, but sometimes I don’t want to bare my entire midriff. That’s where an oversized workout top like this one comes in clutch. I especially love it in white because it's just a touch see-through, so it lets me show off my matching sports bra and workout short combo without feeling exposed. It’s also perfect for those days when I feel a little bloated and just need something loose-fitting that won’t emphasize my stomach.

Unlike the other workout tops you’ll find here, this tee is made from 100% cotton. The natural fiber is not exactly known for its high-performance abilities at the gym (it doesn’t wick sweat very well), but the thinner construction and super boxy fit help keep things super airy. I wore it for an outdoor workout over the summer and felt cool and comfortable—well, as much as you can while doing burpees.

It’s also just a really cute shape. I love the sleeves, which, despite being those of a t-shirt, hit at about the elbow, giving it a really laidback feel. I love it for working out or for throwing on over my skin-tight sets to and from Pilates, but I also find myself grabbing it day-to-day for errands and casual outings. I frequently throw it on over a bright tank styled with some longline biker shorts and comfy sneaks for a cool-girl fit that basically feels like I’m wearing pajamas.

As with any oversized workout tee, it might not be the wisest choice for HIIT workouts or anything super tactical. The billowing sleeves and loose fit could get caught on equipment or flop over your face while bending or jumping.

An open-back top is not only a super stylish choice, but it helps keep you cool as a cucumber during sweaty workouts too. I especially love this top for hot Pilates when I want as little fabric against my skin as possible. And since it has built-in padding (that doesn’t shift around in the wash!), I can literally just wear this on its own to yoga, Pilates, strength training, or other low-impact workouts.

I have worn this during my more intense exercise like an Orangetheory class or while running, and it does offer enough support for me (as someone who teeters between a C cup and a D cup). But if you have a larger chest size, it might be best to reserve this top for low-impact movement or layer it over your favorite sports bra.

Nike’s Dri-FIT tech (a blend of nylon and spandex) is also a major pro. It feels sleek and smooth against the skin but also helps move sweat away from the body. When I leave an intense workout class (even a heated one), it’s noticeable how much less sweat I have sitting between my skin and my workout top when I reach for this one, which is huge for me, since I’ve been struggling with eczema that gets worse with heat and sweat.

The material is also suuuper stretchy and comfortable, and never gets in the way of any kind of movement, whether that’s mat Pilates or an intense upper-body session at the gym. It’s also really lightweight so it feels nearly like a second skin and never requires adjustments mid-workout.

This tank from Gymshark pairs perfectly with the brand’s bestselling leggings. Like the leggings, this tank is nearly seamless—the only seams are along the bottom hem, but they are super flat and don’t cause any rubbing or chafing when up against the skin.

I love that the stretchy, smooth fabric (made of 96% nylon and 4% elastane) is basically sweat-proof and dries super quickly. That’s because nylon is a synthetic fabric that’s hydrophobic (i.e. it resists the penetration of water), so this top is great for wicking moisture away from the body during intense workouts.

Not only that, but it’s super cute, too. I love the square neckline and the length that hits right at the hip bones. It also has a built-in shelf bra to help support and lift the girls for a more flattering shape and a little extra protection against bounce during your workouts. It might not be enough support for larger chest sizes during high-intensity movement, but for smaller chests and moderate activity, it does the trick.

We’ve all been in those super stuffy gyms. When I start overheating during a workout, all I want is to be in a sports bra. But I’m not always comfortable showing my stomach. That’s where the Wild Thing Bra comes in. With its longline fit, which ends just above my belly button for slightly more coverage than a standard sports bra, the top leaves me feeling cool and comfortable at the gym.

And, of course, it’s super cute, thanks to the ruching in the center of the bra. I find this detail really flattering—it gives my stomach a snatched look when I wear it. While it doesn’t offer a ton of support since it’s on the lighter side, it provides decent compression for my higher intensity workouts. Its lightweight design and stylish details make it perfect for pairing with leggings at the gym, but I’ve also seen it styled with trousers or jeans for a sporty yet upscale vibe.

Worried about the lighter colors looking sheer? Don’t be! All styles come with removable cups to cover your girls, which is also helpful because you can take them out when you wash the bra. Speaking of washing, we find that this bra holds up well after multiple washes and never pills or changes in elasticity and shape.

One thing to keep in mind is that the straps aren’t adjustable, which can be a bit frustrating since it means you can’t customize the fit. I also wish it came in more colors.

This tank won the top spot in our Best Workout Tank Tops story for a few reasons: It's super flattering, never rides up, is compressive, supportive, and sweat-wicking.

We tested this ribbed tank across many different workouts—running, yoga, lifting, and HIIT—and we found that it never moves or rides up. And, we love that it’s a tighter spandex tank with high compression, as it holds us in all the right places and doesn’t allow for any boob bounce. It doesn’t have a built-in bra, but it’s tight enough to hold the chest in place.

It's also super moisture-wicking. WH assistant fashion editor Rose Lauture wore this during an intense workout and said there were no sweat stains, no matter which color she wore, thanks to the soft nylon. Because it's moisture-wicking, it also does a great job at preventing body odor.

This option offers some pretty solid support for not having a built-in bra (it's all about the compression!). However, it is made for medium support, so we like to wear an extra bra underneath this tank from time to time when our workouts get extra intense.

Stewart’s pro tip? For high-impact or high-intensity workouts, look for materials that are shiny and smooth to reduce chafing and wick sweat. For lower-intensity workouts, look for matte fabrics that have a soft, buttery texture for comfort and flexibility.

Should your workout top be loose or tight? While it does come down to personal preference, there are pros and cons to each. Tighter tops don’t get in the way of movement as much as a looser top might: they often feel more secure and supportive. But if you find looser tops more comfortable, they can certainly work for nearly every workout except for those involving a Pilates reformer (where loose fabric can easily get caught) or other equipment like cable machines.

Some workout tops have built-in shelf bras or bra pad inserts, but this can be a “love it or hate it” situation, says Stewart. For bigger busts or high-intensity activities, a built-in bra may not provide enough support, so you might need an extra sports bra underneath. However, for smaller busts, we find that they provide ample support for light- and medium-intensity workouts. “A built-in bra should feel supportive and not bothersome and shouldn’t be too tight or digging in to restrict your movement,” says Stewart.

There are tons of workout tops out there, so even finding the absolute best options to test was difficult. When I began the November 2026 update of this article, I revisited our original February 2024 story to see which of the picks our team is still wearing. Some of them are still team favorites, but I went back to the drawing board and asked fitness experts and stylists, including style contributors Kristen Saladino, Rose Lauture, and Lily Wohlner, which workout tops they were loving. From there, I removed the picks that we are no longer wearing and added the options we’ve been reaching for the most.

I made sure that the final picks on this list were options that we wear across all sorts of activities, from compressive options perfect for HIIT workout classes to lightweight, flowy tops we like for lounging or lower-impact exercise. Some of the contenders on this list come in tons of different colors and styles, have built-in bras, and are made with the highest-quality materials for their price points.

#4725. Janus Electric secures battery supply deal for its battery-swap semi truck

Australian conversion specialists Janus Electric have been celebrating a growing slate of orders for their Class 8 electric truck conversions, which ditch diesel in favor of advanced battery-swap electric power – but exactly how they’d deliver all those trucks was still a question. Now, we have an answer: Electrovaya will supply the batteries.

The concept of dropping an electric power unit into a Class 8 semi makes perfect sense, as most of these trucks are built as gliders. That is, rolling body and chassis without an engine and transmission that’s ready to receive power from Cummins, Detroit, International, or Volvo Penta. That’s the role that Janus Electric sees itself occupying, and it seems to be working.

Janus’ reservation book crept past 70 units this past summer, helped along in part by California’s HVIP Program and the US EPA’s Diesel Emission Reduction Act (DERA) Grants. When the HVIP voucher is combined with the Port of Los Angeles’ “Plus” support, customers can received up to $166,000 per truck conversion. Factor in the massive fuel savings of electric and the classic good looks of square-nose Western Star truck body, and it’s easy to see why they’d be a popular choice.

As Jerry Seinfeld taught us however, it’s one thing to take a reservation – it’s another thing to deliver. To help make it happen, Janus has inked a battery supply deal with Electrovaya that will see a $26 million initial purchase orders for Electrovaya battery packs to demand for Janus’ products in the US and Canada, along with the battery company purchasing approximately $1.4 million in Janus stock with (what seems to be) actual money.

“Electrovaya is an important partner to Janus Electric, and we’re particularly pleased it has decided to invest directly in our business,” explains Ben Hutt, Managing Director and CEO of Janus Electric. “The investment is a strong vote of confidence in our technology and approach to electrifying heavy transport.”

The Janus Electric-repowered trucks carry a stout, 480 hp electric motor drawing power from a standard 310 kWh battery pack, with up to two battery packs (one on each side) of the truck. In practice, that gives the Janus trucks up to 370 miles of loaded range. After that, the batteries can be DC fast charged in under 90 minutes, or swapped for fresh ones in about four minutes without too much in the way of specialized equipment. That’s not just Janus’ killer app, it means that a battery supply deal like this one with a strategic partner who’s invested in the fledgling company’s success is such a huge deal.

“Reliable battery supply is critical to our growth,” adds Hutt, “and Electrovaya’s expanding North American manufacturing capabilities will be important as we scale. Both companies see considerable opportunity in this market, and we look forward to building on our partnership.”

For their part, Electrovoya executives seem to know their role here, and seem excited to be a part of what Janus is doing. “Class 8 trucking is one of the most exciting and demanding frontiers in electrification, and Janus has demonstrated real commercial traction with fleets in the US, Canada and Australia,” said Dr. Raj Das Gupta, CEO of Electrovaya. “Janus has developed a practical solution to one of the major challenges facing heavy transport, enabling diesel-powered trucks to be converted to electric without compromising their commercial operations.”

Electrovaya will be expanding its American manufacturing capacity with lithium-ion cell, module, and battery pack production at its new, potentially BABA-compliant facility in Jamestown, New York, which is expected to come online in 2027.

#4724. The Tyranny of Romantic Possibilities

After years or decades, problems and patterns can become deeply entrenched. Be a fly on the wall during a sample couples therapy session and witness the slow, deliberate work of changing those patterns for a more enduring love.

Self Tests are all about you. Are you outgoing or introverted? Are you a narcissist? Does perfectionism hold you back? Find out the answers to these questions and more with Psychology Today.

Posted November 14, 2026 | Reviewed by Abigail Fagan

James Gibson's influential notion of perceptual affordances refers to the meaningful possibilities for action that the environment offers us. A chair affords sitting, a path affords walking, and a door affords entry. I suggest that this concept can also illuminate the romantic realm. Just as the physical environment presents opportunities for action, the romantic environment presents opportunities for attachment, intimacy, desire, and betrayal. Understanding romantic affordances can help us better understand modern love.

At the heart of Gibson's ecological approach (1979) is the claim that we directly perceive possibilities for action rather than constructing them through complex inferences. Affordances are neither purely objective nor purely subjective; they emerge from the relationship between a person and the environment. Importantly, they do not disappear simply because we fail to notice them. A chair still affords sitting even when no one is sitting on it. Affordances are enduring possibilities waiting to be realized.

This perspective also highlights human freedom. Affordances offer possibilities, not necessities. They present opportunities, while leaving us free to decide which ones to pursue (Ben-Ze'ev, 1981).

"When your heart is on fire, you must realize, smoke gets in your eyes." —The Platters

The romantic environment is rich in affordances. A smile may afford intimacy. A glance may afford hope. An attractive stranger may afford the possibility of a new relationship. While Gibson's affordances involve possibilities for action, romantic affordances also involve possibilities for emotional and relational engagement.

A possibility is not the same as a reality. We are often attracted not to who a person is, but to what they might become in our lives. Sometimes we fall in love with a future rather than with a person. Unlike physical affordances, romantic affordances are notoriously ambiguous. We usually know whether a chair can support our weight. We rarely know whether another person's affection is genuine, fleeting, or merely imagined. Yet this uncertainty is often precisely what makes romantic possibilities so seductive.

Consider the familiar strategy of playing hard to get. By appearing simultaneously available and unavailable, interested and uninterested, people create competing affordances. A related assumption is that "whoever makes the first move loses." In both cases, people hesitate to appear overly eager. Ambiguity heightens desire because the outcome remains uncertain.

People are naturally drawn to what remains unresolved. The incomplete, uncertain, and partly unattainable often generates more emotional intensity than what is secure and stable. Romantic ambivalence thrives on such uncertainty. Robert Greene's (2001) portrait of the master seducer rests on this principle. Mixed signals, delayed gratification, and partial fulfillment keep multiple romantic possibilities alive at once. The attraction often lies less in what has been achieved than in what still seems possible (Ben-Ze'ev, 2024; and here).

"You can't hurry love, oh, you just have to wait. Love don't come easy, it's a game of give and take." —The Supremes

"My lover brings me tranquillity. Not during our lovemaking, which is so exciting, but as an enduring sense of inner peace." —A married woman

Modern life has dramatically expanded the number of romantic affordances surrounding us. Dating apps, social media, and increasing social mobility constantly expose us to potential alternatives. At first glance, this freedom seems desirable. Yet, as Barry Schwartz (2009) argued, an abundance of choice can become a burden. When attractive alternatives are always visible, satisfaction becomes harder to achieve. Instead of appreciating what is good enough, we keep searching for something better.

This abundance also fuels romantic ambivalence. The awareness of alternatives can undermine commitment to existing partners. Research suggests that attraction to attractive alternatives increases uncertainty about one's current relationship and diminishes both personal and relational well-being. The irony is striking: More romantic opportunities may generate greater excitement, but not greater happiness (Zoppolat et al., 2024).

Paradoxically, in a world overflowing with romantic possibilities, calmness and patience become increasingly valuable qualities of profound love (Ben-Ze'ev, 2019). A survey conducted across 116 countries and territories found that 72% of adults preferred a calm life to an exciting one, whereas only 16% preferred the opposite. The appeal of calmness extends far beyond romance.

When possibilities are abundant, the ability to devote oneself to a single relationship becomes especially valuable. Calmness and patience are therefore more than pleasant emotional states. They are ways of resisting the tyranny of endless alternatives. Such calmness is not passive. As Shunryu Suzuki (1970) observed, "Calmness of mind does not mean you should stop your activity. Real calmness should be found in the activity itself."

"True love is not a strong, fiery, impetuous passion. It is, on the contrary, an element calm and deep." —Ellen G. White

Modern romance confronts us with a paradox: freedom can become a burden. The more possibilities we perceive, the harder it may be to appreciate and cultivate the relationship we actually have. Romantic affordances create possibilities. Ambiguity makes them more alluring and their abundance makes commitment more difficult. Mature love requires choosing among them.

Indeed, one of the greatest challenges of contemporary love may not be finding romantic opportunities but resisting them. Never before have so many alternatives been so visible and so accessible. Yet no life, and no love, can flourish by pursuing every possibility. The deepest relationships are built not by maximizing options but by limiting them. A meaningful life and a profound love depend less on keeping doors open than on deciding which door to walk through. In modern romance, the greatest threat may not be the absence of opportunities, but the inability to stop pursuing them.

Ben-Ze’ev, A. (1981). J. J. Gibson and the ecological approach to perception. Studies in History and Philosophy of Science, 12, 107–139.

Ben-Ze’ev, A. (2019). The arc of love: How our romantic lives change over time. University of Chicago Press.

Ben-Ze’ev, A. (2024). Romantic affordances: The seductive realm of the possible. Philosophical Psychology, 37, 1762-1796.

Gibson, J. J. (1979). The ecological approach to visual perception. Houghton Mifflin.

Greene, R. (2001). The art of seduction. Penguin.

Schwartz, B. (2009). The paradox of choice. HarperCollins.

Suzuki, S. (1970). Zen mind, Beginner’s mind. New York.

Zoppolat, G., et al. (2024). It’s complicated: The good and bad of ambivalence in romantic relationships. Emotion, 24(5), 1190.

#4723. Romesh Ranganathan, 48, Lost 44 Pounds by Keeping Fitness Simple—Here's How He Made Exercise Stick

The comedian says strength training, running and consistency—not vanity—have transformed his health.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Funny and self-deprecating on screen, Romesh Ranganathan takes his health and fitness seriously off it. He's not your typical gym-goer, though. Rather than training to build a bodybuilder's physique or hit performance milestones, his focus is on staying strong, healthy and active as he gets older—and being there for his three sons.

“I got a medical when I turned 40 as I started to worry about my own mortality, not for myself, but because of my kids,” he told On: Yorkshire Magazine. “Before, when I was going to the gym or staying on top of fitness, I'd do it for some sort of vanity reason. I've long since abandoned that and have accepted that I'm never going to look good. So the second half is about my reaction to that medical.”

Now 48, Ranganathan revealed on the Wolf & Owl podcast that he's been training more consistently in recent months. He has previously said he lifts weights three or four times a week—sometimes more if his schedule allows—while also trying to keep his daily step count high.

“I started hitting the gym for weights about three to four times a week, sometimes more if I fancied, and was trying to up my step count and cardio, but my appetite for that is a struggle,” he said in an interview with Huel.

It's an approach that has helped him lose around 44 pounds over the past few years.

Running has also become a key part of his fitness journey. After initially hating it, the comedian went on to complete the London Marathon in both 2024 and 2025.

The turning point came after one piece of simple advice.

“Running is something that people had always recommended to me. But as soon as I had a go at it, I found it unbearable. I'd go out for a run and be blowing after two minutes, then start walking, run a bit more, start blowing again. I'd come back and just feel absolutely battered,” he told Runner's World.

“Then somebody gave me the basic tip of just slowing down a little bit and getting on top of my breathing. That is the single most helpful tip I've ever had; suddenly I went from someone who couldn't face running to seeing all of the benefits of it. That's not to say that it suddenly became easy.”

Ryan is a Senior Writer at Men’s Health UK with a passion for storytelling, health and fitness. Having graduated from Cardiff University in 2020, and later obtaining his NCTJ qualification, Ryan started his career as a Trainee News Writer for sports titles Golf Monthly, Cycling Weekly and Rugby World before progressing to Staff Writer and subsequently Senior Writer with football magazine FourFourTwo.

During his two-and-a-half years there he wrote news stories for the website and features for the magazine, while he also interviewed names such as Les Ferdinand, Ally McCoist, Jamie Redknapp and Antonio Rudiger, among many others. His standout memory, though, came when getting the opportunity to speak to then-Plymouth Argyle manager Steven Schumacher as the club won League One in 2023.

Having grown up a keen footballer and playing for his boyhood side until the age of 16, Ryan got the opportunity to represent Northern Ireland national futsal team eight times, scoring three goals against England, Scotland and Gibraltar. Now past his peak, Ryan prefers to mix weightlifting with running – he achieved a marathon PB of 3:31:49 at Manchester in April 2025, but credits the heat for failing to get below the coveted 3:30 mark…

A dry, itchy scalp can seriously mess with your day-to-day life. Beyond the maddening urge to scratch, there's the embarrassing component: dandruff and big white flakes studding your strands. And while dermatologists say that a dry, flaking scalp may be a sign of a medical condition called seborrheic dermatitis (this requires a prescription treatment like Zoryve), the best scalp moisturizers—hydrating shampoos for dry scalp, conditioners, and serums—can help.

"I always recommend starting with a gentle, sulfate-free shampoo that cleanses without stripping the scalp of its natural oils and following that up with a hydrating conditioner," says Ross Kopelman, MD, a hair transplant surgeon at Kopelman Hair Restoration in New York City. You can then follow that up with a leave-in treatment or a scalp oil to really lock in moisture.

It's also a good idea to limit hair washing to two to three times a week. "I suggest washing your hair with lukewarm water instead of hot and avoiding excessive heat styling, which can make things worse," Kopelman says. Before adding a few scalp moisturizers to your routine, here's what you should consider before shopping.

Below, shop the six best scalp moisturizers for all hair types, tested by editors and beauty experts.

The Women's Health team is regularly testing scalp moisturizers, and we found it's hard to beat this scalp serum from The Ordinary because of the exceptional value it offers. Yes, it's well-priced, but both dermatologists and testers alike love it. "It's great because it uses hyaluronic acid to deeply hydrate without being greasy," Dr. Kopelman says. He also notes that it's suitable for all hair types, including fine, medium, and thick hair, whether straight, wavy, curly, or coily.

Since I find myself constantly scratching my scalp throughout the day, I added this scalp serum to my hair routine, and after a few days of using it, I found that my symptoms significantly improved. Plus, as an added bonus, my thick, wavy hair appeared shinier and felt softer.

Our testers also like that this The Ordinary product is a leave-in treatment, too, since that makes application quick and easy (meaning there's no need to only use it on wash day).

Like our top overall pick, this is a convenient leave-in treatment. Users like the tingly sensation from the eucalyptus leaf extract, too, telling WH it not only feels refreshing but also smells great.

Our editors can't get enough of Briogeo's hair products—from the shampoo to hair masks, we love just about everything the brand puts out. This scalp moisturizer is no exception. It's powered by antioxidant-rich rosemary oil that supports scalp circulation and healthier hair follicles, castor oil for hydration, and tea tree to fight flakes and reduce itchiness. We love that you can tailor the treatment to suit your preferences—use it as a pre-shampoo rinse (a wait time of 10 to 15 minutes) or use it as an overnight hair mask. Either way, testers found the pointed tip on the bottle very easy to use, saying it made for a much more precise application.

If you have fine hair and want to avoid greasy-looking strands, reach for OUAI's scalp serum. When you have a dry scalp, it's also very important to avoid sulfates. "Sulfates, while great at creating a lather and deep clean, can be drying for the hair and scalp," Dr. Mian says.

#4721. Energica rises from the ashes with plans for cheaper electric motorcycles

The Italian electric motorcycle maker, which ceased operations in 2024 after entering judicial liquidation, has announced a major revival under new international ownership. And while the Energica name is returning, the company behind it is going to look quite different this time around.

Perhaps the biggest change is where the motorcycles will actually be built.

Energica says motorcycle production is moving to Asia, while design, engineering, research and development, as well as responsibility for technical and quality standards, will remain in Italy. The new manufacturing setup is expected to significantly reduce production costs, allowing Energica to cut motorcycle prices by around 20% compared to its previous models.

That could be a big deal for a company whose motorcycles were widely praised for their performance and technology, but were also firmly positioned at the premium end of the market.

The revival comes after Energica was acquired by Energica Pte. Ltd., a Singapore-based company backed by international private investors. Importantly, much of the technological know-how isn’t disappearing overseas with the manufacturing. Energica says its core engineering and design leadership remains in Italy, including longtime CTO Giampiero Testoni and designer Paolo Imeni.

The first motorcycle to make its comeback will be the Energica Experia, the company’s adventure-oriented electric sport-tourer. After that, Energica plans to progressively restart production of the Ego, Eva Ribelle, and EsseEsse9, eventually bringing its entire previous lineup back to market.

At least initially, those motorcycles will use their existing platforms, which should help Energica get bikes rolling off the production line faster without having to develop and homologate entirely new machines. But upgrades are already planned, including a new battery and improvements to range, efficiency, performance, and reliability.

Energica is also specifically targeting Europe, the United States, and Australia as it rebuilds its dealer and service networks. Existing owners haven’t been forgotten either. The company says service has already resumed and spare-parts shipments have restarted to dealers in several countries.

For anyone who followed the electric motorcycle industry over the last decade, Energica’s disappearance was a particularly painful one. This wasn’t some startup with a couple of renderings and a dream. Energica built some of the highest-performance electric motorcycles on the road and spent four seasons supplying the motorcycles for the FIM MotoE World Cup, experience that helped develop its high-voltage and DC fast-charging technology.

Now the company gets something relatively rare in the motorcycle industry: a second chance.

And if moving production to Asia really can knock around 20% off Energica’s prices while retaining the Italian engineering that made the bikes special in the first place, Energica 2.0 might have a considerably better shot at turning great electric motorcycles into a sustainable business.

It seems like moving toward Asian manufacturing is all but inevitable here. It was the expensive European manufacturing of low-volume motorcycles that weighed so heavily on Energica’s balance sheets in the years up to their financial troubles, and so shifting production to countries with both the expertise and the cost benefits for motorcycle manufacturing simply makes sense.

Energica isn’t alone in discovering the economics of moving electric motorcycle production to Asia. Zero Motorcycles spent years manufacturing its bikes in California before beginning a major shift toward production in the Philippines in 2023, including both complete motorcycles and major subassemblies. Now the company works with multiple factories, including major manufacturers like Zongshen in China, to reduce production costs for its electric motorcycles while still maintaining the ‘designed in California’ marketing angle.

It’s too early to tell how the new strategy will play out for Energica, but the fact that the company is now following a more well-worn trail is a positive sign for those who have spent the last two years hoping for a revival.
